metadata.title: Dareke Young (hamstring) upgraded to full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Dareke Young (hamstring) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: It looks like Young should be good to go this week, as he was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday after being limited by a hamstring injury on Wednesday. He's not expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

metadata.title: Dareke Young (hamstring) limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Dareke Young (hamstring) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Young is now listed on Las Vegas' injury report due to a hamstring issue of some kind and was limited at practice on Wednesday as a result. It could leave him sidelined for Week 3, but even if that's the case, fantasy managers shouldn't expect much change in Las Vegas' offense as a result.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - Questionable to finish game
metadata.description: Young (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Young exited the second half of Sunday's contest due to a hamstring injury. The wide receiver is the fifth option for the Raiders offense, with sixth option Cody White recording two touchdowns Week 2. It is unclear how significant Young's injury is.

metadata.title: Dareke Young signs with Raiders
metadata.description: The Raiders signed WR Dareke Young to a contract.
metadata.analysis: Young follows Klint Kubiak from Seattle to Las Vegas. He should remain primarily in a role on special teams.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - Heading to Vegas
metadata.description: Young is in line to sign with the Raiders, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The wide receiver, who dealt with a quadriceps injury in 2025, caught two passes for 48 yards and no scores across nine regular-season games. Young saw action more often on special teams than on offense.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - Career year in 2025
metadata.description: Young caught two of three targets for 48 yards and tallied 322 kick-return yards across nine regular-season games in 2025.
metadata.analysis: The fourth-year pro from Lenoir-Rhyne set career highs in receiving yards and kick-return yards while tying his best reception total, all while appearing in just nine regular-season contests. Young also operated as one of the Seahawks' top special-teamers, logging 156 snaps and tallying nine total tackles  during the regular season. Set to become an unrestricted free agent this offseason, Young could draw interest from teams seeking special-teams help ahead of next season.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - Key special-teams play
metadata.description: Young recovered a fumble and made a tackle in Sunday's 31-27 win over the Rams in the NFC Championship Game.
metadata.analysis: Young played just one offensive snap as the team's No. 5 wide receiver, but he made a massive play on special teams, recovering a muffed punt in the third quarter. Seahawks WR Jake Bobo caught a 17-yard touchdown pass on the next play. Young has been an outstanding gunner on special teams this season and will look to make a similar impact in the Super Bowl versus the Patriots.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - No targets in blowout win
metadata.description: Young wasn't targeted in Saturday's 41-6 win over the 49ers in the divisional round.
metadata.analysis: Young worked as the No. 5 wide receiver and logged just 11 offensive snaps. He has received just two targets this season, so his work will be most noticeable on special teams in the NFC Championship Game.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - Targeted once in win
metadata.description: Young didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Young logged 11 offensive snaps -- his largest total since Week 3 -- because Rashid Shaheed (concussion) and Cody White (groin) exited the game early and didn't return. The Seahawks face a crucial test in Week 18 with the No. 1 seed on the line against the 49ers, and Young could have a slightly increased role once again if Shaheed and White can't go.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - No offensive reps
metadata.description: Young didn't play an offensive snap in Thursday's 38-37 overtime win versus the Rams.
metadata.analysis: Young missed the last seven games with a quadriceps injury, and his role in Week 16 was limited, as expected. The 2022 seventh-round pick is the No. 5 wide receiver in the rotation and won't be a dependable option down the stretch.

metadata.title: Dareke Young - Activated for Thursday's game
metadata.description: Young has been activated from injured reserve and does not carry an injury designation for Thursday's home game against the Rams, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Young has been a full participant at practice throughout Seattle's preparations for Thursday Night Football, so it's unsurprising to see him activated in time to face off against Los Angeles. After having missed the Seahawks' last seven games due to a quad injury, Young will now resume handling a depth role in the team's wide receiver corps.
